text.en:
On Republic Day Maya saw the words "India, that is Bharat" on a poster.
"Why two names?" she asked her grandfather.
"Both are our country's names," he said. "One comes from a river and one from an old king."

Our country has more than one name. India, Bharat and Hindustan are all used. The Constitution says: India, that is Bharat.
The name India comes from the River Indus, called Sindhu in Sanskrit. Foreign travellers pronounced it Hind or India. Bharat is an ancient name found in old texts and linked to the king Bharata.
India lies in the Northern Hemisphere. In the north are the Himalayas. In the south the land narrows into a peninsula surrounded by the Indian Ocean, with the Bay of Bengal in the east and the Arabian Sea in the west.
India has many landforms: mountains, plains, plateaus, deserts, coasts and islands. Great rivers such as the Ganga, Yamuna, Godavari and Kaveri flow through it.
India is divided into states and union territories. Its capital is New Delhi.
Our country has two official names: India and Bharat. The Constitution says India, that is Bharat.
The name India comes from the River Indus, known as Sindhu. Bharat is an ancient name.
The Himalayas are in the north. In the south, the land is a peninsula with seas on three sides.
India has mountains, plains, plateaus, deserts, coasts and great rivers. Its capital is New Delhi.

problem.en: Where does the name India come from?

text.en: It comes from the River Indus, called Sindhu.

why.en: Travellers named the land after the river.

text.en: The word Sindhu changed to Hind and then India.

why.en: Names change as people pronounce them differently.

text.en: So India is named after the Indus river.

prompt.en: A friend says Bharat is a new name given recently. What will you say?

requiredIdeas.en: Bharat is an ancient name found in old texts.
The Constitution uses both India and Bharat.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking Bharat is a new name.

points.en: India, Bharat and Hindustan are names of our country.
India comes from the River Indus; Bharat is ancient.
The Himalayas lie in the north and the Indian Ocean in the south.
